roadmapTask:
Plan horizon 2 of the agent-agnostic-browser-bridge project (tools/chrome-bridge/). Horizon 1 shipped the standalone package: protocol (PAGE_ACTIONS single source of truth), standalone ws relay on 127.0.0.1:8766, the standalone MV3 extension with the 7 page actions (navigate, getPageText, readPage, findElement, clickElement, typeText, captureTab), the controller client, and the stdio MCP server with one tool per page action.

Horizon 2 scope, in priority order:
1. readConsoleMessages and readNetworkRequests: capture page console output and page network requests (fetch/XHR) from the real Chrome tab into bounded per-tab ring buffers held in the extension, and expose them as two new page actions / MCP tools with a `since` + `limit` query parameter (queryable ring buffer with clear-since semantics). This needs a MAIN-world page script (console/fetch/XHR wrapping), an ISOLATED content script forwarding to the service worker, the build plumbing for those two extra entries in the plain-Vite extension build, and wiring through PAGE_ACTIONS / TOOL_CATALOG so the tsc parity mechanism covers them. These are guaranteed in this horizon.
2. The multi-client README MCP config snippet verified by hand against two non-Claude clients. Installed on this machine: Gemini CLI, Crush (charmbracelet crush CLI), and the Cursor app; Codex CLI is NOT installed. Verify with Gemini CLI + Crush; document Cursor and Codex config shapes. Only if it fits in the phase budget; otherwise defer to horizon 3.
3. Size-cap tuning: empirical check of response sizes (readPage 200k-char default, captureTab image block) against the clients. Lowest priority; defer if it does not fit.

User decisions from scoping: capture delivery is PULL-ONLY (entries accumulate in extension-side ring buffers and are returned only by the two read tools; no observation-frame streaming to controllers, no tail CLI in this horizon). Capture tools come first; README/size-cap spill to horizon 3 if the horizon exceeds ~5 phases.

dimensionScores.evidence: Hand-written predicate (no as/satisfies/!) checks every field of both shapes: separate null-accepting vs undefined/wrong-type rejection for status/contentType/bodyPreview, and console-shaped entry under channel network is rejected via the paired isConsoleEntry/isNetworkEntry guards. A 9 would loosely handle nullable fields or the pairing.

boundText measures UTF-8 bytes with TextEncoder, returns input unchanged under the cap, and truncates on code-point boundaries (for...of) so byte length is always <= maxBytes; handles 2/3/4-byte chars and the maxBytes=0 edge. A 9 would be untested against surrogate pairs; emoji case keeps the pair whole at 4 bytes.

CaptureEnvelope is a two-member discriminated union so env.entry.requestId typechecks under network and errors under console; grep confirms nullable fields are | null (no ?:), CAPTURE_NAMESPACE is as const, level/channel string-literal unions. A 9 would have a nullable field declared optional.

Every export named verbatim and behaviour asserted; factory helpers (withoutEntryField, consoleEnvelope, networkEnvelope) mutate exactly one field per negative case, both channels have accept (toBe(true)) and reject (5+ distinct toBe(false)) cases, plus 3 boundText assertions incl. a byte-length check. A 9 would share a hand-copied fixture.
